--- title: Skill Gap Analysis --- ## Team Skills vs. Market Demand (2024 Postings) ### Market demand from job postings ::: {#0b7ac6b6 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import pandas as pd import seaborn as sns import matplotlib.pyplot as plt jobs = pd.read_csv("data/jobs.csv", usecols=["SKILLS_NAME", "SOFTWARE_SKILLS_NAME"], low_memory=False) text = (jobs["SKILLS_NAME"].fillna("") + " " + jobs["SOFTWARE_SKILLS_NAME"].fillna("")) # display name -> search pattern in the skills text patterns = { "SQL": r"\bSQL\b", "Python": r"Python", "Tableau": r"Tableau", "Power BI": r"Power BI", "Excel": r"Microsoft Excel", "Data Visualization": r"Data Visualization", "Data Analysis": r"Data Analysis", "ETL": r"Extract Transform Load|\bETL\b", "Statistics": r"Statistics|Statistical Analysis", "Machine Learning": r"Machine Learning", "Cloud (AWS/Azure)": r"Amazon Web Services|\bAWS\b|Microsoft Azure", "Communication": r"Communication", } demand = pd.Series({ name: text.str.contains(pat, case=False, regex=True).mean() for name, pat in patterns.items() }).sort_values(ascending=False) demand_pct = (demand * 100).round(1) demand_pct.rename("% of postings listing skill").to_frame() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: ::: {#f89ab570 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} plt.figure(figsize=(8, 5)) sns.barplot(x=demand_pct.values, y=demand_pct.index, color="#2C7FB8") plt.xlabel("% of postings listing the skill") plt.title("Most In-Demand Skills in Business Intelligence Postings") plt.tight_layout() plt.show() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![](skill_gap_analysis_files/figure-html/cell-3-output-1.png){width=765 height=470} ::: ::: ### Team skill levels Scale: 1 = Beginner, 2 = Basic, 3 = Intermediate, 4 = Advanced, 5 = Expert. ::: {#d38697d1 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} # EDIT: replace names and scores with your real team's team = { "Name": ["Richa", "James", "Ben", "Victoria"], "SQL": [4, 3, 3, 2], "Python": [4, 3, 4, 2], "Tableau": [2, 3, 1, 2], "Power BI": [2, 2, 1, 3], "Excel": [4, 4, 3, 4], "Data Visualization": [3, 3, 2, 3], "Data Analysis": [4, 4, 3, 3], "ETL": [2, 1, 1, 2], "Statistics": [3, 3, 4, 2], "Machine Learning": [3, 2, 3, 1], "Cloud (AWS/Azure)": [2, 1, 1, 2], "Communication": [4, 4, 3, 4], } df_skills = pd.DataFrame(team).set_index("Name") plt.figure(figsize=(10, 4.5)) sns.heatmap(df_skills, annot=True, cmap="coolwarm", linewidths=0.5, vmin=1, vmax=5) plt.title("Team Skill Levels Heatmap") plt.tight_layout() plt.show() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![](skill_gap_analysis_files/figure-html/cell-4-output-1.png){width=860 height=429} ::: ::: ### Skill gaps Required level is scaled from market demand: the most-demanded skill maps to 5, and others scale proportionally. A gap is the required level minus a member's level (0 if they meet it). This is a relative measure, not an absolute standard of expertise. ::: {#5a11aaa7 .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} required = (demand / demand.max() * 5) gap = (required - df_skills[required.index]).clip(lower=0).round(1) plt.figure(figsize=(10, 4.5)) sns.heatmap(gap, annot=True, cmap="Reds", linewidths=0.5) plt.title("Skill Gaps vs. Market Demand (higher = bigger gap)") plt.tight_layout() plt.show() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![](skill_gap_analysis_files/figure-html/cell-5-output-1.png){width=869 height=429} ::: ::: ::: {#b4c9b7d8 .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} summary = pd.DataFrame({ "Team average": df_skills.mean().round(1), "Market-required level": required.round(1), "Average gap": gap.mean().round(1), }).sort_values("Average gap", ascending=False) summary ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=5} ```{=html}
